note: Rewritten from the species-level description in Sands (1972); original in English; the genus has no soldier caste and only alates and workers are described; measurement tables, figure numbers, type specimens and distribution records are not translated; one composite ratio is omitted because an OCR separator is missing.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The smallest species of the genus. Compared with all the other species except A. polyscolus; the latter has longer mandibular apical teeth in both castes, a more conspicuous fontanelle in alate and worker, and worker enteric valves with fully developed spinose armature, in which cushion 3 is elongate and bears long comb-like spines. The worker abdomen of A. nanus appears to be dehiscent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule and pilosity pale yellow, setae sparse. Postclypeus moderately raised, Pcl/W 0.27–0.31, Pcl/Ri 2.20–2.75. Mandibular apical teeth rather long, La/Li 0.69–0.73, Ra/Ri 0.82–0.88; the accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible is just separated from the molar prominence in surface view, composite ratio 14.81–16.20; the tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible is distinctly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth markedly shorter than that of the second, composite ratio 20.50–20.70. Fore tibia moderately inflated, Ti/Tw 3.61–3.78, the third apical spur about half the length of the other two. The midgut-hindgut overlap is longer than four times the midgut width at the attachment of the Malpighian tubules; the enteric valve base is sessile, attached directly to the second hindgut pouch, very weakly bilobate, dorsolateral in the undissected abdomen; the enteric valve cushions are of roughly equal development and protrude slightly from the valve opening, the surface scaly, the scales in the posterior third of the cushions developed into small to conspicuous spines; the valve wall bears rather many minute spines between and outside the inner cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule brown (the colour perhaps partly faded), not distinctly darker above the fontanelle; fontanelle minute, oval, flat, slightly paler than the head colour; the median spot oval, about as large as the fontanelle, set on a small tubercle and slightly raised, concolorous with the head; postclypeus slightly paler than the head colour, labrum yellow; frontal mark a flat crescent, concolorous with the head; antennae pale yellowish brown. Pronotum and meso- and metanotal plates pale brown, transverse sutures present; femora and tibiae yellow, tarsi pale yellow. Abdominal tergites pale brown, dorsal spiracles paler; sternites and ventral spiracles very pale brown; cerci yellow. Posterior margin of head capsule nearly evenly circular; ocelli medium-sized, separated from the compound eye by from slightly more than half their minimum diameter to nearly their full minimum diameter; postclypeus moderately raised, Pcl/W 0.29–0.32, posterior margin evenly circular, median suture present and weak in some specimens. Mandibular apical teeth moderately long, La/Li 0.67–0.76, Ra/Ri 0.84–1.00; the accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible is just separated from the molar prominence in surface view; the tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible is distinctly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth shorter than that of the second, composite ratio 21.1–23.9. Head capsule pilosity fairly even, a slightly rough felt, with erect setae, brown.
